title: Environment Protection (Sea Dumping) Amendment (Using New Technologies to Fight Climate Change) Bill 2023
short_title: Environment Protection (Sea Dumping) Amendment (Using New Technologies to Fight Climate Change) Bill 2023
portfolio: Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill updates Australian law to align with international rules that allow carbon dioxide to be sent overseas for storage under the seabed and permit certain ocean-based climate experiments.

It would create two new permit types: one for exporting captured carbon dioxide for burial in geological formations beneath the sea floor, and another for placing materials in the ocean for marine geoengineering research.
The bill also makes small adjustments to existing rules and updates the language of the law, without adding any new fees or changing who enforces the rules.
changes: Introduces permits for exporting carbon dioxide streams for sub-seabed storage.
Introduces permits for placing wastes or other matter for marine geoengineering research.
Makes consequential amendments to support the new permits.
Makes technical updates to simplify the law's wording.
summary.affected: Companies and researchers involved in carbon capture, export, and marine geoengineering, as well as the agency that issues sea dumping permits.
